name: Little River Dispersed Camping
note: 15 numbered high-elevation sites along the Little River, suitable for tents and small to medium RVs.  The narrow gravel road may be tricky for larger rigs.  Very remote with no cell service.  Sites fill up on weekends.  --AWH  Reviews (2020-23, all 5*): about half the ~16 numbered sites on FR 17 take a trailer, and a side loop of 5 gravel-pad sites (turnoff between sites 6 and 7) is the trailer pick. It's often empty even on weekends, while the riverside sites fill. Largest rig reported is a 36-ft fifth wheel, but the road is narrow, potholed and muddy after rain, with tight turns onto one-lane bridges. Sites 9 and 13 are called the prettiest, with small pools and a gravel beach ~50 yd below 9, and wildflowers, ferns and grassy spots at the water. Fire rings and a few tables; no trash service. Daytime helicopter and low-level military jet noise is a recurring complaint. An aggressive black bear was reported in 2023, so keep food locked in the vehicle. --Claude

note:
Often described in reviews as the best dispersed camping in WV.  Approximately 20 high-elevation campsites with breathtaking mountain views, dark skies, and significant distance between sites.  Sites range from tent-only spots to big group sites.  Sites 12, 14 and 16 are particularly sought-after for their views and privacy.  Extremely remote and not likely to be crowded.  The gravel road is maintained but may be steep and rough in places.  Reviews indicate no problems for 22-25 ft trailers and a 39-ft converted school bus.  Limited cell signal may be available near site 1.  --AWH and Claude

note: Campground in a wooded setting surrounded by live oaks, about a half mile walk to driftwood beach. --AWH

booking.note: NOT in the Georgia State Parks reservation system, despite Jekyll Island calling itself a state park: booking is Campspot or 912.635.3021, not gastateparks.reserveamerica.com, so the state:GA booking window and 4pm cutoff do not apply here. Three-night minimum on Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day, with holiday rates; no general minimum. 'We only offer daily rates, with the maximum stay allowed being 14 nights.' Check-in from 2pm, check-out by noon. Boats and utility trailers must go into storage rather than on the site.

fees.note: THE ISLAND ENTRY FEE IS THE TRAP, and the campground says so itself: 'the parking fee collected at the entrance gate is separate from the campsite reservation fee, and must be paid for each day on the island.' It is mandatory for every vehicle entering Jekyll - $10 per day, '$15 for vehicles exceeding 8' ' (which is most RVs), plus $5 more on designated special-event days (Independence Day, Shrimp & Grits Festival, Holly Jolly Jekyll). Annual is $100, or $150 oversized. per is vehicle_DAY, unlike the Georgia state parks ParkPass, which an overnight guest pays once for the whole stay - a week here is 7 gate days on top of the site. A GEORGIA PARKPASS IS NOT VALID and earns no discount: the Authority's own discount list names CCGA students, state-government vehicles, public school buses and disabled veterans (free annual pass, service-connected VIC/VHIC, redeemed in person) and explicitly not GA State Parks pass holders. Jekyll 'does not receive operational dollars from the State of Georgia like other State Parks', which is why it gates its own fee. Rates are 'from' figures: the cheapest site a 23-ft motorhome fits is the full-hookup back-in from $51 (primitive tent sites from $36 take only small self-contained rigs 'depending on size'), pull-through from $54, yurts from $125; the hookup premium is not published as a separate surcharge so none is recorded. One-time $4 pet fee per pet (tent/RV sites). Cancelling 7+ days out costs $25; inside 7 days it is higher, and an early departure is also $25.

inclusion_evidence: Operator westboggs.com: '154 campsites that accommodate tents and RVs', active reservations -> real RV campground

fees.note: Two people, one night: $40. There is no camping fee; the cost is Colorado Parks and Wildlife's State Wildlife Area pass, which everyone 16 or older needs on the property. 2 people x 2 one-day passes x $10 = $40: a one-day pass is valid only on the date printed on it, and a night spans the arrival and departure dates. Nobody holding an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license needs the pass, and neither do under-16s. An annual SWA pass is $43.87 (March 1 to March 31 of the next year; youth/senior $11.96). The pass is per person, not per vehicle; buy it online or in the My CPW app, up to 60 days ahead. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

inclusion_evidence: recreation.gov 232463: RMNP drive-in campground, 247 sites across 5 loops, RVs to 40 ft, electric+standard+tent sites, currently reservable
waterfront_evidence: not waterfront -- satellite: forested bench, Big Thompson R. >600m N behind a ridge.
note: Rocky Mountain NP campground in Moraine Park, the Big Thompson River meadow below the high peaks. About 236 sites in five loops, 46 of them electric; rigs up to 40 ft, many sites tent- or van-sized and many not level. Flush toilets, dump station, solar shower stalls (bring your own bag). Reservation only in summer, first come first served in winter, when it is the park's only open campground. Rangers may enforce keeping RV windows closed due to bears. --Claude

sites.note: 236 bookable sites in the recreation.gov catalog (46 electric) plus 22 management sites. Vehicles over 40 ft, including tow vehicle and hitch, are not permitted; many sites are for tents or vans only, so check each site's length.

facilities.note: Two solar shower stalls: campers bring their own solar shower bag, no water in the stalls. Dump station and fresh water fill near the ranger station, open in winter too. Firewood sold in summer.

booking.note: Summer season: reservation only on recreation.gov (no in-person booking), some sites up to 6 months ahead and some on short-term release; the reservation includes the Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road permit from 1 p.m. on arrival day. Winter season: first come, first served, paid by Scan & Pay or at an entrance station. Summer limit is 7 nights in total across all RMNP campgrounds.

name: Newaygo State Park Campground
inclusion_evidence: MI DNR Newaygo SP 99-site rustic drive-in campground on Hardy Dam Pond, large sites fit 23-ft rig, reservable via midnrreservations.com
waterfront_evidence: audited 2026-06 (MI state evidence-gate sweep, commit 35f5f25); waterfront 'not waterfront' set by that satellite/per-site-map sweep (per-entry bucket detail in the commit message)
note: Rustic campground in two loops (Oak #1-48, Poplar #49-99) atop 20-ft embankments overlooking Hardy Dam Pond, a 6-mile flooding of the Muskegon River; large private sites with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers. Boat launch between the loops with a few mooring spots for registered campers, buoyed swim area in the Poplar loop, kayak rentals at the office early June to mid-September, 18-hole disc golf; borders the Manistee National Forest. Spongy moth larvae can surge in summer. --Claude

sites.note: 99 rustic campsites in two loops, Oak (#1-48) and Poplar (#49-99), with 20- to 30-ft forested buffers between them. Allowed rig lengths on the booking site run 25-50 ft; all but 3 take 30 ft or more. No pull-throughs listed.

facilities.note: Drinking water and trailer fill at the one-lane sanitation station near the campground office.

facilities.note: Drinking water and a place to fill trailers with potable water, but no dump station. Lighthouse gift shop sells some camping supplies.

booking.note: Fully self-contained RVs only. ReserveAmerica, up to 12 months ahead and for the same day. As of October 2026, 2027 reservations are on hold while RIDEM picks a new reservation provider, so the channel and rules may change. Unreserved sites are let first come at the parks. STAY LIMIT: 7 nights in any 21 days in peak season (the Thursday before Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend), then 14 nights away; 21 nights in 28 the rest of the year. RIDEM's full policy also sets peak-season minimum stays, not recorded here. Check-in 1-10 p.m. (no later, reserved or not), check-out 11 a.m.; the permit holder is 18 and stays on the site; one family, or six people, a site; two vehicles. The site must be occupied the first night or it is resold with no refund. CANCELLING: 8 days or more before arrival, everything back but the reservation fee and an $8.75 cancellation fee; 2 to 7 days, one night is kept as well; under 2 days, no refund. No refunds for weather or leaving early.

booking.note: A NIGHT HERE CANNOT BE BOOKED - reservable false is about the nightly sites; the fair-week packages below are the only thing that takes a reservation. Run by the South Dakota State Fair, not GFP, so none of the state-park policy applies - no park entrance licence, no 90-day window, no 4 p.m. check-in, and the $16/$23 GFP rates are not these rates, which is why this entry declines the registry. During the fair the only nightly camping is Lot J, self-contained, no hookups, about 40 sites: 'Sites are first come-first serve... No reservations are taken for nightly camping.' You pay at the Gate 13 gate house on arrival. The hookup sites are sold as a fair-week package only (6 nights plus 4 gate passes), booked by phone with the Fair Administration Office, and renewals from previous years are offered before new reservations open on June 1. Camping outside fair week is arranged separately with the same office.

fees.source: https://www.sdstatefair.com/general-information/guest-services/camping/

fees.note: 'The price for nightly camping is $25/night starting on the arrival date' - that is the fair-time, self-contained, no-hookup Lot J rate, paid at the gate. The rate for the hookup sites is not published: they are sold only as a package. No park entrance licence is charged or valid here. No campfires or open fires anywhere on the fairgrounds, propane fire pits included.

name: Devil's Elbow Campground
waterfront_evidence: pin was mis-placed ~0.9km NW on arid slopes; real Devil's Elbow campground is the peninsula at 46.7004,-111.8055 with RV loops ringing an open, sparsely-vegetated shoreline of Hauser Lake - pads on open aprons at the waterline on both sides of the peninsula
inclusion_evidence: BLM devils-elbow-campground page + Recreation.gov #272276: 48 gravel pads accommodating RVs/trailers, reservable -> real drive-in RV campground
note: BLM (Butte Field Office) recreation area on the Devil's Elbow of Hauser Lake, ~12 mi NE of Helena off York Road (paved); every site looks over the lake, but there is little shade. Concrete boat launch with courtesy dock, small beach; marina, store with gas and a bar/restaurant half a mile away. --Claude

sites.note: 48 sites with level gravel pads, five of them tent-only, plus group Loop C with a reservable ramada. 36 RV sites list a 60-ft maximum on recreation.gov. Up to 2 camping units per site, each paying the nightly fee.

facilities.note: Drinking water in peak season (BLM: 'As of January 2025, there is no running water at the site'). No dump station. Fish cleaning station; boat slips complimentary for registered campers.

booking.note: The description says 'All sites are reservation only', but a recreation.gov notice says 'First-come, first-served sites are available in this campground' and the rate table has walk-in seasons in April and October-November around the May-September reservation season. You must occupy the site every reserved night and cannot change sites. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am. 14 nights in a rolling 30 days.

waterfront_evidence: satellite at 41.1108,-106.0122: Laramie River lined by continuous dense riparian treeline; RV/trailer area set back on west behind the tree belt -> not waterfront
inclusion_evidence: Operator woodslanding.com Accommodations page: 10 RV sites with electric+water hookups and a sewer dump, plus store/bar-grill -> real transient drive-in RV park (private)
note: Historic roadside resort ~20 mi SW of Laramie on the Laramie River near Medicine Bow NF: 10 RV sites with electric+water hookups and a separate sewer dump, most with picnic table/fire ring; also cabins, a store, and bar/grill. --Claude

name: Ayres Natural Bridge Park
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 42.7347,-105.6118: RV/trailers parked on open grassy flats within ~15-35m of LaPrele Creek with open unobstructed bank -> creekside
inclusion_evidence: Converse County parks page + Campendium/allstays for Ayres Natural Bridge Park: county-operated free FCFS park with paved drive-in sites for RVs under 30 ft (23-ft rig fits) -> real drive-in RV campground
note: Converse County-run park in a canyon 11 mi W of Douglas (I-25 exit 151, then ~5 mi S) around one of the few natural bridges with water still flowing beneath it (LaPrele Creek). Free, first-come first-served; a handful of paved pull-in sites for trailers/RVs under 30 ft plus tent sites, with tables, fire rings, vault toilets, water and trash. 3-night limit; day gate 8am-8pm. --Claude

name: Eston Riverside Regional Park

The campground taps are not drinking water, which is sold at the clubhouse and concession.  There is no boat launch (the nearest is at the ferry, about 10 km away), but boats can be beached beside the park. --Claude

name: Nickle Lake Regional Park

note: Regional park on the shores of Nickle Lake and the Souris River near Weyburn, where tall poplars line the road in and each area has a playground; there are shelters and benches along the shoreline, a groomed sandy beach and roped-off swimming area (no lifeguard), an 18-hole mini golf course and, new in 2026, a canteen.  Its 342 sites are 16 tent, 55 full-service and 271 30-amp power-and-water sites, with group camping in a secluded bay and at Crescent Point; some partial-service sites in Riverview are pull-throughs.  Two boat launches and a floating dock serve the lake, which holds walleye, perch and pike, is stocked from time to time and has a fish-cleaning area.  An 18-hole golf course is 3 miles away. --Claude

name: Nine Mile Ranch
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 39.7750,-110.4648: cabins/RV sites on grassy terrace bench; meadow/vegetation between sites and any Nine Mile Creek channel, no open water visible at pads
inclusion_evidence: 9mileranch.com + Campspot booking: multiple 18-site drive-in campgrounds (Kokopelli best for RVs/trailers/vans), pull-through + back-in, no hookups, reservable -> real drive-in RV campground
note: Working cattle ranch of Ben Mead and his daughter Carla in Nine Mile Canyon, 24 paved miles up Nine Mile Canyon Road from Wellington and a gateway to the canyon's petroglyphs; its campgrounds are the only camping allowed in the canyon.  Its campgrounds sit beside Nine Mile Creek with plenty of shade and green grass; every site has a picnic table and a fire pit or ring, and every campground a spring-water faucet.  Kokopelli is best for RVs, trailers and vans, Cottonwood Hollow is mostly for tents, small vans and truck campers, and the Turnouts are pull-throughs.  Showers ($3) are at the main ranch, and generators are off from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. (9 p.m. in fall).  The ranch also rents settler cabins rebuilt on the property and bed-and-breakfast rooms.  There is no cell service in the 50-mile canyon, and Wi-Fi only around the main house. --Claude

name: Fish House Inn & RV Park
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 44.4676,-119.5351: in-town RV park; John Day River ~150m+ east across fields and a treed corridor, sites not on the bank
inclusion_evidence: Official fishhouseinn.com/rv-parking + Campspot listing: 15 full-hookup drive-in grassy RV sites with easy back-in access, reservable -> real transient RV park
note: Country inn and RV park in Dayville, in a craftsman house built in 1908 for the mill owner Walt Greenwell and converted into an inn in 1991, nine miles from the Sheep Rock Unit of the John Day Fossil Beds and the Thomas Condon Paleontology Center.  The seven full-hookup spaces behind the inn are each 60 ft long on level gravel, separated by grass and trees, and the five power-only sites are on the lawn and have picnic tables.  Guests share a community fire pit with a bar and grill, barbecue grills and horseshoe pits; the John Day River, the town park and playground, the Dayville Cafe, the Mercantile and the South Fork Mini Market & Gas are within walking distance, and there are swimming holes nearby.  EV charging costs $10 an hour or $30 a day, and an RV check-in before 2 p.m. costs $10; monthly winter rates, November through April, are by phone.  The inn also has rooms and an Airstream Bambi for glamping. --Claude

Utility recreation land = private by convention. --Claude  Road work on Butt-Prattville Road near Cool Springs, Ray Adams Boat Launch and Ponderosa Flat from Aug 10, 2026 through the rest of the 2026 season: traffic delays, heavy trucks, noise and dust (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Rancho Seco Recreational Area
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 38.3308,-121.0960: RV loop encircles a grassy point on Rancho Seco Lake; NW-arc pads overlook the lake across ~55m open grass with a brush/tree band lining the immediate shore, most pads face the marsh - view not on-water
inclusion_evidence: smud.org Rancho Seco page + Campspot booking: 21 electric drive-in RV sites on the lake rim, reservable -> real RV campground (SMUD municipal utility = local)
note: SMUD's 400-acre park around a 160-acre lake fed by the Folsom South Canal, 25 miles from downtown Sacramento, with 21 RV and 32 tent sites and a designated swimming beach.  Weekend stays take two nights, Friday and Saturday together; stays are limited to 14 days, and campers with reservations cannot enter after 10 p.m.  Boat trailers have been banned since March 14, 2025 to keep out the invasive golden mussel, and hand-launched craft are inspected on entry; boats are rented on weekends and holidays from Memorial Day to Labor Day.  The lake holds bass (catch and release only), bluegill, redear sunfish and crappie, and rainbow trout are stocked from November through March.  The Howard Ranch Trail is an easy seven-mile round trip across a working cattle ranch, so dogs stay home.  The park also rents Jupes, and outside firewood is not allowed. --Claude

name: Rideau Acres Campground
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 44.308,-76.423: RV sites within a pad-depth of the Cataraqui/Colonel By Lake shore (shore point with dock + open lawn to water); operator ~8000ft waterfront with boat ramp

note: Large family-operated campground established 1971 at 1014 Cunningham Rd on the Rideau Canal (UNESCO World Heritage waterway) 10 minutes from downtown Kingston. 443 sites — 241 overnight/transient plus 202 full-season — with 322 water/electric/sewer sites, 30 and 50 amp service and pull-throughs; max RV length 45 ft. 2026 nightly rates $51 unserviced, $63 W/E 30 amp, $69 W/E/S 30 amp, $75 W/E/S 50 amp, $83 50 amp premium. Season roughly May 1 to November 1; outdoor pool, lake swimming, boat rentals, mini putt, frisbee golf. Reservable online with a 50% deposit. --Claude

name: Serpent River Campground

note: Campground between Highway 17, the Trans-Canada, and the Serpent River, which empties into the North Shore of Lake Huron, midway between Sudbury and Sault Ste. Marie. name: Kimberley Riverside Campground
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 49.631,-115.998: St. Mary River wraps the campground S/E; southern/eastern RV loops sit on a bench above a treed river bank (sandy cutbank/bluff on the outer W bend) — overlook river but treed bank/bluff buffer, not an open apron

note: Campground beside the St. Mary's River, an 8-minute drive south-west of Kimberley's town centre, the Platzl, with over 150 campsites.  Full-service sites 26-67 and 91-140, in the Mountain View and Pine Meadows areas, take 15- to 50-amp power and rigs of 25 to 45 ft, and the riverview sites 68-79 take 30 or 50 amps and 25 to 35 ft; sites 26, 27, 28, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49, 53-57 and 110-140 are pull-throughs.  The power-and-water back-ins, 1 to 25B (15 or 30 amps, 25 to 40 ft), are closest to the pool and mini-golf, and the non-service sites NS1 to NS9 (20 to 25 ft) are first come, first served.  A free heated pool is open from mid-May to the September long weekend and an 18-hole putting course from early May to late September, and there is a timber picnic shelter, a playground, bocce, horseshoes and sand volleyball.  The Adventure Centre rents e-bikes, stand-up paddleboards and inflatable kayaks and sells Kootenay Rafting Company tours.  Cell service is spotty.  In winter the bathrooms behind the office stay open with running water and hot showers, tanks are filled there from a hose, and the sani-dump is at site 26.  Winter storage costs C$250 from October 1 to April 20.  The campground also rents trailers and trapper's tents and has walk-in tent sites. --Claude

Esri z18 at 45.6455,-61.5823: the loop road runs along both the cobble harbour shore and the cove; north of the entry road is a hay field.
inclusion_evidence: hyclass-campground.com + COANS listing + Campspot booking: 69 sites incl 30-amp full-hookup pull-through RV sites, no seasonal rentals -> real transient drive-in RV campground
note: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites out on the point.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (a US Census rooftop match on the operator's published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west and Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west), and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop. Lewis and Clark passed the "burning bluffs" here. Reservable online. --Claude

name: Delta National Forest Campsites
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 253459): 56 standard drive-in sites, every one reservable and every one stating a length (30-210 ft; all fit 23+ ft), permitted equipment RV/trailer/tent -> real drive-in RV camping. NOT a single campground: the sites are spread along about 12 forest roads across the forest (see note); pinned at Blue Lake Recreation Area, which holds 3 of them. waterfront_evidence: the catalog publishes no per-site coordinates; satellite at the Blue Lake Recreation Area pin shows a small clearing ~30 m from the Blue Lake oxbow under bottomland canopy, and 53 of the 56 sites lie elsewhere along forest roads -> no per-site evidence for any shoreline site, default down
note: Primitive, reservable campsites scattered through the Delta National Forest, the only all-bottomland-hardwood national forest, between Rolling Fork and Yazoo City off MS-16. Not one campground: 56 sites sit in small groups along Forest Service roads 703, 707, 710, 715, 720 and 721, Dummyline Road, the Green Ash and Dowling Bayou greentree reservoirs, MS-16, and the Blue Lake and Little Sunflower River recreation areas (this pin is Blue Lake, 3 sites). Sites are long (30-210 ft, most 60 ft+) and must be reserved before arrival, receipt on site. Four restrooms along FSR 715, 717, 720 and 707; drinking water only at the Delta Ranger District work center on FSR 703; no hookups. The forest is a Wildlife Management Area - no alcohol, busy in hunting season, and the bottomland floods seasonally. ATVs on permitted trails only. Unstaffed; district office 662-873-6256. --Claude

name: AuSable River Campsites - Sawmill Point (Cooke Pond)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 234130, loop Sawmill Point): 15 reservable drive-in sites permitting RVs and trailers, 12 of them 26-30 ft -> real drive-in RV camping (primitive; one cluster of a dispersed system, entered per cluster at AWH's call 2026-09-22)

note: Fifteen drive-in sites on and around Sawmill Point on Cooke Dam Pond, off River Road west of Oscoda; most (045D-057D) ring the point above the pond, while 042D-044D sit among private cabins to the south. inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 233807): 102 standard sites typed RV/trailer; stated lengths where given are mostly 10-22 ft, with a few at 25-40 ft (site 016 is 35 ft); most sites carry no length. Caveat (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 37.2473,-118.5692 with the catalog pads plotted (z18): the creekside row (002-004, 008-010) sits 27-40 m from the South Fork of Bishop Creek, but the creek runs inside a dense riparian forest band that screens the pads -> not waterfront
note: Large Forest Service campground at 8,100 ft on the South Fork of Bishop Creek, west of Bishop on Hwy 168 toward South Lake; trout fishing, a fish-cleaning station, and the Tyee Lakes trailhead under a mile away. 102 sites, mostly small - the published lengths run 10-22 ft with only a few at 25-40 ft (site 016 is 35 ft), so book a site that lists your length. Partly reservable online, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233807/rates (recreation.gov rate table, current seasons, standard/RV sites)

name: Horse Creek Campground (Lake Kaweah)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 233692): 72 standard sites typed RV/trailer, stated 24-50 ft (62 at 25 ft or more), all reservable; rec.gov: 80 sites without hookups, flush toilets, showers, dump station
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 36.3898,-118.9545 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): the imagery is at deep drawdown with the basin dry, but the OSM full-pool line of Lake Kaweah runs 1-4 m from the lower pads, the drawdown rings climb to the loop's edge, and nothing but open ground lies between -> lakefront measured to high water (lake access varies by month, per the rec.gov notice)
note: Corps of Engineers campground on Lake Kaweah three miles east of Lemon Cove, on the way to Sequoia National Park. 80 sites without hookups (published 24-50 ft), flush toilets, showers and a dump station; summer weekend amphitheater programs. The lake is a flood-control reservoir: at full pool it reaches the campground, but through much of the year the water is far off. Reservable online; gate closes at 10 pm (9 pm off-season). --Claude

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/233692/rates (recreation.gov rate table, current seasons, standard/RV sites)

name: RV Village at Camp Richardson (South Lake Tahoe)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 10305470): 98 RV electric sites stated 25-40 ft, all reservable; rec.gov: 20 full-hookup and 78 water/electric RV sites, operated by Camp Richardson Resort on Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit land
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 38.9331,-120.0421 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): RV loops in pines 500+ m from the Lake Tahoe shore across Highway 89 and the resort -> not waterfront
note: Concessionaire-run RV campground at Camp Richardson Resort on Forest Service land at South Lake Tahoe, off Highway 89; beach, marina, bike path and resort amenities within walking distance. 98 RV sites (published 25-40 ft): 20 full hookup, 78 water/electric. Restrooms, showers and the dump station close mid-November to mid-May, though some sites stay open with heated water. Reservable online. Forest-wide 14-day yearly limit. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10305470/rates (recreation.gov rate table, current seasons, standard/RV sites)

name: Upper Oso Campground (Santa Ynez River)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 231961): 3 standard sites typed RV/trailer stated 32 ft plus equestrian, tent and walk-to sites; FS: 10 sites open first-come first-served, the other 14 (mostly equestrian) closed after storm damage
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 34.5570,-119.7718 (z17): the RV sites sit in oak woodland in Oso Canyon with no per-site water flag -> not waterfront
note: Forest Service campground in Oso Canyon above the Santa Ynez River, off Paradise Road north of Santa Barbara; trailheads for the Santa Cruz Trail and the Aliso National Recreation Trail, and the Camuesa OHV route nearby. Only three sites take a trailer or RV (32 ft). PARTLY OPEN: 10 sites first-come, first-served, the other 14 (mostly equestrian) closed after storm damage (FS, checked 2026-09-24). No drinking water. High river levels can close it in winter. --Claude

name: Glory Hole Recreation Area (New Melones Lake)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 234073): 121 standard/RV sites typed RV/trailer, stated 40-90 ft, reservable; Bureau of Reclamation New Melones Lake, 14-day limit
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 38.0086,-120.5405 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): pads on oak-woodland hills 260-300+ m from the OSM New Melones Lake line; rec.gov notes 'water front' sites exist only at high lake levels -> not waterfront
note: Bureau of Reclamation recreation area on New Melones Lake near Angels Camp, the main camping hub on the lake, in foothill oak woodland. About 120 RV sites (published 40-90 ft) plus walk-in tent sites; marina, boat ramps (usable only above 870 ft lake elevation), hiking and biking trails. Reservable online. The dump station has been out of order. Gate closes at 9 pm; 14-day limit within 30 days. --Claude

waterfront_evidence: satellite at 37.9789,-120.5062 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): loops on the hills 300+ m from the OSM New Melones Lake line -> not waterfront
note: Bureau of Reclamation recreation area on New Melones Lake near Sonora and Jamestown: about 100 RV sites with 30-65 ft driveways, plus walk-in sites, and a boat ramp. CLOSED: all Tuttletown campgrounds have been closed since a broken pipe took out the area's water supply in 2024; rec.gov shows every site closed through mid-2027 and Reclamation directs campers to Glory Hole (checked 2026-09-24). --Claude

name: Trimmer Campground (Pine Flat Lake)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 233314): 5 standard sites typed RV/trailer (2 stated 30 ft, 3 at 20 ft) plus 5 tent-only, all reservable; USACE Pine Flat Lake. Only two sites fit a 23-ft rig (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 36.9057,-119.2892 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): the lake is deep in drawdown in the imagery, but the OSM full-pool line of Pine Flat Lake runs 2-11 m from sites 01-03 with open bare slope between -> lakefront measured to high water (the rec.gov notice warns lake access may be unavailable at low water)
note: Small Corps of Engineers campground on the shore of Pine Flat Lake east of Fresno, off Trimmer Springs Road. 10 sites: 5 take RVs, but only two are long enough for a 23-ft rig (30 ft; the rest are 20 ft); 5 tent sites. Reservable online. When the lake is drawn down, lake access from the campground may not be available. 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Big Meadows Campground (Sequoia NF, Generals Hwy)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 256932): 18 RV sites, 12 of them typed RV and stated 28-42 ft, plus 23 tent-only; rec.gov: 43 sites at 7,500 ft, no potable water; partly reservable
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 36.7188,-118.8261 with the catalog pads plotted (z18; canopy-blind): the OSM Big Meadows Creek line passes 14-27 m from several sites, but the pads can't be seen under the fir canopy and no per-site flag or agency map puts them on the creek -> no qualifying source, not waterfront
note: Forest Service campground at 7,500 ft in the Sequoia National Monument on Big Meadows Road off the Generals Highway, between Sequoia and Kings Canyon national parks (not in Shenandoah). 43 sites: a dozen take RVs (published 28-42 ft), the rest are tent sites. NO drinking water. Trailheads into the Jennie Lakes Wilderness; Buck Rock Lookout nearby; Hume Lake 15 miles. Reaching it from Fresno means paying the Kings Canyon entrance fee. Partly reservable. --Claude

name: Hume Lake Campground (Sequoia NF)

waterfront_evidence: satellite at 36.7927,-118.9088 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): loops 330+ m above Hume Lake; rec.gov: 'some of which have views of Hume Lake', with foot trails down to the shore -> lakeview
note: Popular Forest Service campground above Hume Lake at 5,250 ft in Sequoia NF, near Kings Canyon National Park. 68 sites, 47 for RVs/trailers (published 20-35 ft); some have lake views and foot trails lead to the shore. Flush toilets and drinking water. Non-motorized boats only on the lake. Reservable online. --Claude

note: Popular Forest Service campground above Shaver Lake at 5,500 ft in Sierra NF; some sites shaded by fir, cedar and pine, others open with lake views. 42 RV/trailer sites (driveways 28-42 ft) and about 20 tent sites; five trails start from the campground; boat mooring nearby. Reservable online. --Claude

note: Forest Service campground beside Chapman Creek near the North Yuba River on Highway 49 east of Sierra City (Tahoe NF). 19 RV/trailer sites (published 20-45 ft) plus tent sites; the Chapman Creek Trail starts in camp, the Pacific Crest Trail is nearby, and the Sardine Lakes are five miles away. No hookups or showers; no OHVs in camp. Partly reservable, the rest first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Cottage Creek Campground (Bullards Bar Reservoir)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog (facility 10137699): 9 standard sites typed RV/trailer with 50-99 ft driveways, all reservable; FS/rec.gov: a new campground of double and triple sites with paved spurs, 'built with RV camping in mind'
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 39.3980,-121.1479 with the catalog pads plotted (z17): sites on a slope above New Bullards Bar Reservoir; the only water within 30 m is an unnamed drainage. rec.gov: 'a beautiful view of the Bullards Bar Reservoir'; swimming limited by steep slopes -> lakeview
note: New Forest Service campground above New Bullards Bar Reservoir (Tahoe NF) near Camptonville, with views of the lake. 9 double and triple sites with paved spurs (driveways 50 ft and up), built for RVs; the access road climbs at about 8%. Boating, fishing and water skiing on the reservoir; steep shores limit swimming from camp. Marina and supplies nearby. All sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Mecca Flat Campground (Deschutes River)
inclusion_evidence: BLM: 13 individual campsites and a group site, first-come first-served year-round, $8-12/night; Campendium reviews report a 34-ft Class A (2019), a 30-ft travel trailer (2021) and a 26-ft travel trailer (2023) in sites. No agency length (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 44.7695,-121.2078 (z17, z19; no per-site coordinates, pin from the OSM campground outline): the sites sit inside a loop whose west road runs along the Deschutes, with a ~15-25 m grass-and-brush bank strip beyond it; the loop road is between every pad and the river -> riverview
note: BLM campground on the Deschutes Wild and Scenic River just off Highway 26 north of Madras, 1.6 miles down Mecca Flat Road; the south end of the 7-mile Trout Creek Trail along the river starts here. 13 sites and a group site, first-come, first-served year-round; $8/night Sunday-Thursday, $12 Friday-Saturday. Vault toilets, no drinking water, no cell. No length is published, but reviewers have brought a 34-ft Class A and 26-30 ft trailers in. The access road is a narrow single lane with a drop-off and few pullouts - reviewers call it bumpy and nerve-racking with a trailer. Goatheads (puncturevine) in the area. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mecca-flat-campground ('$8.00/night fee applies Sunday through Thursday nights, Friday and Saturday night fee is $12.00/night ... May 15th September 15th', read 2026-10-10)

fees.note: $8/night Sun-Thu, $12 Fri-Sat, May 15-Sep 15 (BLM page).

name: Duncan Reservoir Campground (Silver Lake)
inclusion_evidence: BLM: four single campsites on the west side of Duncan Reservoir and a group site below the dam, first-come first-served, free, open year-round; The Dyrt reviews (2024-25) describe pull-through sites along the reservoir. No agency length (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 43.0695,-120.9465 (z17, z19; no per-site coordinates): the campsite track runs along the open west shore 10-20 m from the water across bare ground and scattered juniper, nothing between; dated firsthand review (Oct 2024) of a 'pull-thru site along reservoir' -> lakefront
note: Free BLM campground on small Duncan Reservoir in the sagebrush west of Silver Lake's dry lakebed: 5 miles east of Silver Lake on OR-31, then 5 miles south on gravel County Road 4-14 (sometimes rough, with washouts that reviewers drove around). Four single sites along the west shore, three of them pull-throughs at the water, plus a group site below the dam; boat ramp, covered picnic area, vault toilet, no drinking water, no food or gas nearby. First-come, first-served, open year-round; stocked trout, ice fishing in winter. Open range - watch for cattle. No published site length. --Claude

fees.source: note prose

name: Big Spring Campground (Ochoco NF)
inclusion_evidence: FS Ochoco NF: 'Campsites at this campground may be the easiest to access with a trailer on the entire forest', though 'size and number of trailer sites limited'; free, open year-round, first-come first-served; RIDB facility pin matches the OSM campsite node. No length published (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 44.3324,-119.9926 (z17): the campground is under ponderosa canopy; the FS mentions a creek alongside but no per-site flag, map or legible image places a pad on it -> not waterfront
note: Small, free Forest Service campground in open ponderosa pine beside a creek in the eastern Ochocos: from Prineville, US-26 east 16 miles, FR 42 past the Ochoco Ranger Station and Deep Creek Campground, then about 5 miles further (also reachable from Paulina). A handful of sites of varying size; the FS calls it perhaps the easiest trailer access on the forest but says trailer sites are limited in size and number, and publishes no length. Vault toilet, no hookups or drinking water, no fee, 14-day limit, open year-round. Cattle graze nearby. --Claude

fees.source: note prose

name: Kokosing Lake Campground (Fredericktown)
inclusion_evidence: operator site kokosingcampground.com: Fredericktown Recreation District campground on the Corps' North Branch Kokosing River Lake, 46 sites with partial-hookup RV, primitive and tent sites, reservations by phone or in person, open 2nd Friday of April to 4th Saturday of October; Campendium reviews (2019-21) put 25-ft Class Cs and a 25-ft travel trailer in sites, 30-amp service
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 40.5079,-82.5854 (z18; campground located from its OSM outline, the RIDB pin sits at the dam outlet 1 km SE): the east loop runs along the lake shore with its RV spurs on the lake side, 10-20 m from the water across mown grass and scattered shade trees, nothing between; reviewer (2019): 'a nice setting right on the water' -> lakefront
note: Campground run by the Fredericktown Recreation District on Kokosing Lake, the Corps of Engineers flood-control lake 1.5 miles northwest of Fredericktown, at 18352 Waterford Road. 46 sites: partial-hookup RV sites with 30-amp electric, primitive and tent sites, several along the shore; showers and restrooms (per reviews), playground, large picnic area and a two-lane boat ramp. Open from the second Friday of April to the fourth Saturday of October. Reservations by phone or in person only - no online booking. Reviewers (2019-21) fit 25-ft Class Cs and trailers; some sites have low branches. One 2020 review mentions a few long-term campers. --Claude

name: Blanchard Springs Campground (Ozark NF)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog for the Blanchard Springs Recreation Area (facility 250010): 17 individual standard sites stated 25 ft, first-come first-served, plus group sites; rec.gov: flush toilets and drinking water, individual sites open except in high water; facility 250871 description: water, dump station, 'sites suitable for smaller RV's and tents', no hookups
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 35.9728,-92.1776 (z18; individual sites carry no coordinates): the loop sits under canopy on the inside of a bend of North Sylamore Creek, with an open sand-and-gravel bar between the trees and the water ~35 m from the pin; rec.gov per-site 'Proximity to Water: Riverfront' on every individual site -> creekside
note: Forest Service campground in the Blanchard Springs Recreation Area (Ozark NF) north of Mountain View, beside North Sylamore Creek under yellow pines and rock bluffs, near Blanchard Springs Caverns and trout fishing at Mirror Lake. 17 individual sites, all 25 ft - a 23-ft rig fits with little to spare - first-come, first-served, plus reservable group sites. Flush toilets, drinking water and a dump station; no hookups. The campground closes when the creek is high: call 870-757-2211 to check. --Claude

name: Black Kettle Campground (Dead Warrior Lake)
inclusion_evidence: FS Cibola NF & National Grasslands: Black Kettle Campground, 12 camping units, vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables; The Dyrt review (Oct 2021): 'Large parking area where you can park an RV'; free, first-come first-served. No published site length (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 35.7452,-99.7143 (z17): the campground loop sits in the trees below the Dead Warrior Lake dam, ~140 m from the dam and farther from the water, with the embankment between -> not waterfront
note: Free Forest Service campground on the Black Kettle National Grassland, below the dam of 80-acre Dead Warrior Lake, 9.9 miles north of Cheyenne on US-283. 12 camping units under mature trees; vault toilets, potable water from pumps set back from the parking area, tables, fire rings. First-come, first-served. No site length is published; reviewers describe a large parking area that takes an RV, but most sites are on a slope. Canoeing and fishing on the lake. Watch for ticks, and the red soil stains. --Claude

fees.source: note prose

name: Lower Virginia Creek Primitive Campground (Conway Summit)
inclusion_evidence: FS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Bridgeport RD): 'several sites can accommodate large trailers or motorhomes', vault toilets, bear boxes, no fee, late May-mid October; RIDB facility 243885 (no site catalog); pinned on the OSM campground node, ~450 m from the RIDB pin, which sits in the meadow
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 38.0637,-119.2275 (z18): sites strung along a gravel spur in Jeffrey pine, ~100 m from Virginia Creek with forest between -> not waterfront
note: Free, primitive Forest Service campground at about 9,100 ft in Jeffrey pine off Virginia Lakes Road near Conway Summit, south of Bridgeport: US-395 south 13 miles, right on Virginia Lakes Rd for 2.4 miles, then left on FR 139. The FS says several sites take large trailers or motorhomes. Fire rings, bear boxes, vault toilets; no water, trash service or hookups - pack it out. First-come, first-served, late May to mid-October; fills on summer weekends. A free California campfire permit is required for any fire or stove. --Claude

fees.source: note prose

name: Centerville Flat Dispersed Campground (Markleeville)
inclusion_evidence: FS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Carson RD): dispersed camping area at CA-4 and Wolf Creek Road with existing spots 'for camping (tent, trailer, RVs)', vault toilet, horse corral, free, open year-round; Campendium review (June 2020) in a 25-ft Class C. No published length (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 38.6322,-119.7218 (z17): dispersed spots on a pine-and-sage bench ~140 m from Silver Creek and farther from the East Fork Carson River below -> not waterfront
note: Free Forest Service dispersed camping area on a bench above the East Fork Carson River at the junction of CA-4 and Wolf Creek Road, 2.5 miles up CA-4 from CA-89 south of Markleeville. Existing spots for tents, trailers and RVs, a vault toilet and a horse corral; no water. Open year-round as conditions allow. A reviewer brought a 25-ft Class C (2020) and warned the rocky dirt roads are hard for big fifth wheels and Class As. No cell service. A free California campfire permit is required. --Claude

fees.source: note prose

booking.source: Forest Service dispersed camping is first-come with no reservation system (no fee, no permit: 16 U.S.C. 6802(d)(1)(C),(E)); same check as provenance.fees

name: South Area Campground (Conchas Lake, USACE)
inclusion_evidence: RIDB per-campsite catalog under facility 10086087 (the gap row 248170 is its recreation-area record): 20 standard nonelectric sites typed RV/trailer, no lengths; rec.gov: '20 primitive camp sites with water only, picnic shelter, grills, and fire pits', $10, water April-November; October 2026 calendar shows sites available. No published length (see note)
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 35.3777,-104.1927 (z17; the catalog carries no per-site coordinates): terraced loops on the south shore of Conchas Lake, the upper row's shelters ~20-40 m above a rocky ledge shoreline with the loop road along it; open view over the lake but the shore is rock bank, not a walk-in apron -> lakeview
note: Corps of Engineers campground on the south side of Conchas Lake in eastern New Mexico, across the lake from the state park's north side (federal passes apply only here). 20 primitive sites with water, a picnic shelter, grills and fire pits, $10/night; water April-November only. Reservable online. No site length is published, but every site lists RVs and trailers. AT&T is the only working cell carrier. --Claude

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10086087/rates (recreation.gov rate table, current seasons, standard/RV sites)

name: Nineteenmile Campground (Chiwawa River)

name: Jordanelle State Park - Hailstone Campground
waterfront_evidence: satellite at 40.6180,-111.4255 (z18), viewed 2026-09-29: the southern loop's road runs 20-40 m above Jordanelle Reservoir's waterline, but the open sand between it and the water is a used day-use beach (swimmers, with a day-use parking strip just west), so the apron is not unused; lake fully visible from the loop -> lakeview. OSM: 208 m from the pin to the reservoir polygon
inclusion_evidence: utahstateparks.reserveamerica.com site catalog (parkId 342471, pulled 2026-09-29): 119 drive-in STANDARD sites - 98 water + 30 or 30/50-amp electric, 21 full hookup (30/50 amp, sewer) - with max vehicle lengths mostly 55-80 ft (27 at 60 ft); plus 36 drive-in tent sites, hike-in/boat-in primitive sites at Rock Cliff and the reservoir, cabins; stateparks.utah.gov/parks/jordanelle (2026-09-29) lists camping, electricity, dump station -> real drive-in RV campground
note: Hailstone, the main recreation area of Jordanelle State Park, on the west shore of Jordanelle Reservoir off US-40 exit 8, a few miles from Park City and above the Heber Valley. About 120 RV sites in several open loops - most with water and 30 or 30/50-amp electric, 21 full hookup - many long enough for big rigs, plus tent sites, cabins, marina, swim beach, dump station and a designated International Dark Sky Park. Little shade. Construction outside the park boundary was audible in 2026. Rock Cliff (east end, walk-in tent) and Ross Creek are separate areas. Reservable on Utah State Parks' ReserveAmerica site. --Claude

fees.note: Two people: $20. There is no camping fee here; what it costs is Montana FWP's Conservation License, which everyone 12 or older needs to use a fishing access site: $10 per non-resident, so $20 for two. It is an annual license (March 1 to the end of February), so it also covers every other night at Montana fishing access sites and wildlife areas that license year. Residents pay $8 (youth 12-17 and seniors 62+ $4); anyone with a Montana fishing license already has one, and under-12s need none. Buy it online at ols.fwp.mt.gov, at an FWP office or from a license agent. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)

note: Franchise Jellystone Park in the woods outside Grayling.  A site may share its water and electric pedestal with another, so extension cords and extra hoses may be needed, and sewer sites are limited.  There is a pool (no lifeguard), a jumping pillow, mini golf, a Silent Disco (new in 2026) and a Bear Factory; day passes cost $15 a person, Sunday to Thursday, and early check-in $35.  The person booking must be 21 and a site holds one immediate family; e-bikes, EV charging and outside firewood aren't allowed, nor are golf carts for overnight guests.  Two dogs at most; quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m.  Cabins and RVs are rented. --Claude

fees.source: https://cpw.state.co.us/swa-finder (everyone 16+ needs an SWA pass or a hunting/fishing license; one-day pass $10, valid only on its date; annual $43.87; license exemptions) and https://cpw.state.co.us/state-wildlife-areas/south-republican-swa (camping in designated areas, no camping fee listed); two people, one night per AWH 2026-10-11

fees.note: Two people, one night: $40. There is no camping fee; the cost is Colorado Parks and Wildlife's State Wildlife Area pass, which everyone 16 or older needs on the property. 2 people x 2 one-day passes x $10 = $40: a one-day pass is valid only on the date printed on it, and a night spans the arrival and departure dates. Nobody holding an annual Colorado fishing, small-game, big-game or turkey license needs the pass, and neither do under-16s. An annual SWA pass is $43.87 (March 1 to March 31 of the next year; youth/senior $11.96). The pass is per person, not per vehicle; buy it online or in the My CPW app, up to 60 days ahead. (AWH 2026-10-11: price as two people, one night.)
